titleEn: The Song of the Cid — Jerome made bishop; Minaya's embassy wins leave for Ximena; the Infantes take notice (tiradas 78–82, lines 1287–1384)
part: Tiradas 78–82 · Jerome made bishop; Minaya's embassy wins leave for Ximena; the Infantes take notice (lines 1287–1384)

sentences.i: While all were rejoicing at this news, there came from the East a man of the tonsure: the bishop Don Jerome is the name he bears.
sentences.n: Tirada 78 (assonance á-o) — Don Jerome comes to Valencia (Pidal: Don Jerónimo llega a Valencia). Line-ends alegrando, coronado, llamado, acordado … gradescamos, obispado, mandados: á-o throughout. En estas nuevas todos se alegrando: a gerund clause with the pronoun before it (se alegrando = alegrándose), 'all rejoicing at this news' (the Çid's plan to bring his wife and daughters, last tirada). Pidal's note to v. 1288: coronado, 'clérigo', 'cleric' (compare v. 1501): literally 'crowned', from the clerical tonsure (corona). de parte de orient, like Latin ex orientis partibus, ab Eois partibus, was a vague phrase used in Castile for the origin of monks and priests who came from north of the Ebro to restore the monasteries and churches; said of Valencia, Pidal remarks, it is inexact for a French cleric, as don Jerónimo was. Jero[me]: the me is Pidal's (in italics); his headings call him Jerónimo. el obispo: the poet gives him the office he is about to receive (v. 1303). so = su.

sentences.t:
Bien entendido es de letras e mucho acordado,
de pie e de cavallo mucho era arreziado.
sentences.l:
Well understood he-is in letters and much prudent,
on foot and on horse much he-was hardy.
sentences.i: He was well versed in letters and of sound judgement, and on foot or on horseback a man of great strength.
sentences.n: entendido de letras, 'learned in letters', i.e. educated, as a cleric should be. Pidal's note to v. 1290: acordado, 'que obra con acuerdo y madurez; cuerdo, prudente', 'one who acts with judgement and maturity; sensible, prudent'. de pie e de cavallo, 'on foot and on horseback': he can fight as well as read. arreziado, 'strong, vigorous', a participle-adjective akin to rezio (= recio, 'strong'); Pidal gives no note. es … era: present and imperfect side by side, the usual tense-mixing.

sentences.t:
Las provezas de mio Çid andávalas demandando,
sospirando ques viesse con moros en el campo:
que sis fartás lidiando e firiendo con sus manos,
a los días del sieglo non le llorassen cristianos.
sentences.l:
The prowesses of my Çid he-was-going-about-them asking,
sighing that-himself he-might-see with Moors in the field:
that if-himself he-sated fighting and striking with his hands,
to the days of-the world not him might-weep Christians.
sentences.i: He had gone about seeking word of my Çid's deeds of prowess, sighing to find himself face to face with Moors in the field: for if he could take his fill of fighting and striking with his own hands, then for all the days of the world let no one weep for him.
sentences.n: Las provezas … andávalas demandando: the object put first and taken up by las; andar + gerund, 'went about asking after, kept seeking'. provezas = proezas, 'deeds of prowess'. ques viesse = que se viesse, 'that he might see himself, find himself' with Moors in the field: the se squeezed onto que; viesse, imperfect subjunctive of veer. sis fartás = si se fartás: fartarse (= hartarse, f- for h-), 'to take one's fill'; fartás is the imperfect subjunctive with its final -e cut (= fartasse; compare quebrantás, v. 34). firiendo, from ferir (= herir), 'to strike'. a los días del sieglo, 'to the days of the world', i.e. ever; with non, 'never' (sieglo = siglo, 'world, age'). Pidal's note to v. 1295: cristianos, 'nadie', 'no one' (compare v. 29). llorassen, imperfect subjunctive of llorar, here 'to weep for, mourn'. The sense seems to be that, once he had fought the Moors to his heart's content, he would die satisfied and need no mourning; the poem does not spell it out, and the exact force of the clause is uncertain.

sentences.t:
Quando lo oyó mio Çid, de aquesto f[o] pagado:
“Oíd, Minaya Albar Fáñez, por aquel que está en alto,
quando Dios prestar nos quiere, nos bien gelo gradescamos:
sentences.l:
When it heard my Çid, of this he-was pleased:
“Hear-ye, Minaya Albar Fáñez, by Him who is on high,
when God profit us wishes, we well to-Him-it let-us-be-grateful:
sentences.i: When my Çid heard of it, he was well pleased: “Hear me, Minaya Álvar Fáñez, by Him who is on high: when God is minded to favour us, let us give Him due thanks for it.
sentences.n: lo oyó, 'heard it', Jerome's longing. f[o] = fue, its o Pidal's (in italics), as so often: de aquesto f[o] pagado, 'was pleased at this' (pagado, 'pleased, satisfied', not 'paid'; aquesto = esto). Oíd, imperative 2nd pl. of oír. aquel que está en alto, 'Him who is on high' (as at v. 8). prestar, 'to benefit, be of use to': prestar nos quiere, 'is willing to do us good', the pronoun nos standing before the infinitive's governing verb. gradescamos, present subjunctive 1st pl. of gradesçer, 'let us be grateful': nos bien gelo gradescamos, 'let us thank Him well for it' (ge lo, 'to Him it'; this nos is the subject, 'we').

sentences.i: In the lands of Valencia I mean to found a bishopric and give it to this good Christian; and you, when you go to Castile, will carry good tidings.”
sentences.n: fer quiero obispado, 'I wish to make a bishopric': fer, a short form of fazer (= hacer); quiero governs both fer and dárgelo. dárgelo = dar + ge + lo, 'to give it to him' (ge, the ancestor of modern se). ides = vais, present for future, 'when you go'; levaredes = llevaréis, future 2nd pl. of levar, 'to carry'. mandados, 'tidings, news': the founding of a see is news to bring the king.

sentences.i: Álvar Fáñez was pleased with what Don Rodrigo said. To this Don Jerome they grant forthwith the office of bishop; they gave him a see in Valencia, where he may well be rich.
sentences.n: Tirada 79 (assonance í-o) — Don Jerome made bishop (Pidal: Don Jerónimo hecho obispo). Line-ends Rodrigo, obispo, rico, cristianismo, obispo, vinos. Plogo, preterite of plazer: Plogo a Álbar Fáñez de lo que …, 'it pleased Álvar Fáñez, what …'. don Rodrigo, the Çid's own name. yal = ya le, 'now … him', le squeezed onto ya. otorgar por obispo, 'to grant (him) as bishop', confirm him in the office. Present and preterite again side by side (otorgan, diéronle). diéronle, 'they gave him': what was given is not said, presumably the see and its endowment; o = donde. Valencia without the cedilla here, as Pidal prints it. Pidal's note to v. 1302: the Cid himself, de su mano (v. 1332), makes the bishop. In the first times of the Reconquest kings created bishoprics and named bishops; in fact, after Jerónimo's election as bishop of Valencia by the Cid and his men, Pope Urban II and the metropolitan of Toledo, don Bernardo, intervened to consecrate him canonically, as the charter of endowment of the church of Valencia, granted by the Cid in 1098, attests.

sentences.t:
¡Dios, qué alegre era tod cristianismo,
que en tierras de Valençia señor avie obispo!
Alegre f[o] Minaya e spidiós e vinos.
sentences.l:
God, how glad was all Christendom,
that in lands of Valençia lord there-was bishop!
Glad was Minaya and took-leave-himself and came-away-himself.
sentences.i: God, how glad was all Christendom that in the lands of Valencia there was a lord bishop! Glad was Minaya; he took his leave and set out.
sentences.n: tod = todo, its last vowel dropped before a vowel (tod el, v. 1318). cristianismo, 'Christendom', the Christian people. señor … obispo, 'a lord bishop'; avie (= había) is here impersonal, 'there was'. spidiós = espidió se, 'took his leave' (espedirse), with the initial e- dropped in the print; vinos = vino se, 'came away, set off' (venirse): the enclitic squeeze twice in one half-line. f[o] = fue again.

sentences.t:
Tierras de Valençia remanidas en paz,
adeliñó pora Castiella Minaya Álbar Fáñez.
sentences.l:
Lands of Valençia remained in peace,
headed for Castiella Minaya Álbar Fáñez.
sentences.i: The lands of Valencia left at peace, Minaya Álvar Fáñez made straight for Castile.
sentences.n: Tirada 80 (assonance á) — Minaya heads for Carrión (Pidal: Minaya se dirige a Carrión). Line-ends paz, contar, fallar, ha, fallar, allá, a stressed á; Fáñez (twice) counts with them, its unstressed last syllable disregarded. Tierras … remanidas en paz: a participle clause standing on its own, 'the lands of Valencia (being) left in peace'; remanidas, past participle of remaner, 'to remain'. adeliñó, 'headed straight' (adeliñar, v. 1203). pora = para.

sentences.t:
Dexarévos las posadas, non las quiero contar.
Demandó por Alfonsso, do lo podrie fallar.
sentences.l:
I-will-leave-to-you the lodgings, not them I-want to-recount.
He-asked for Alfonsso, where him he-could find.
sentences.i: His halts on the road I will pass over; I have no wish to tell them. He asked after Alfonso, where he might find him.
sentences.n: Dexarévos = dexaré + vos, the future of dexar (= dejar) with vos glued on after it: 'I will leave (them) to you', i.e. pass them over — the minstrel speaking to his hearers. posadas, 'lodgings', the stages of the journey. Demandó por, 'asked after'. do = donde; podrie = podría, conditional 3rd sing.; fallar = hallar (f- for h-).

sentences.t:
F[o]ra el rey a San Fagunt aun poco ha,
tornós a Carrión, i lo podrie fallar.
sentences.l:
Had-gone the king to San Fagunt yet little it-has,
returned-himself to Carrión, there him he-could find.
sentences.i: The king had gone to Sahagún a little while before; he had come back to Carrión, and there he could find him.
sentences.n: F[o]ra = fuera, its o Pidal's: the -ra form as a pluperfect indicative, 'had gone' (ser lends its past to ir, as fue, 'went'). aun poco ha, 'only a little while ago' (ha = hace, 'it has (been)'). tornós = tornó se, 'came back' (tornarse). i = 'there' (as at v. 1150), not 'and'. Pidal's note to v. 1312: San Fagunt is today Sahagún, 35 kilometres west of Carrión; the two towns are joined by the camino francés, the road to Santiago. Alfonso VI was drawn there by the great Benedictine monastery, a devotion inherited from his father Fernando I; defeated by his brother, he had had to take the monk's habit at Sahagún in 1072, escaped from there to live among the Moors of Toledo, and afterwards favoured the monastery continually, giving it his body for burial.

sentences.t:
Alegre f[o] de aquesto Minaya Álbar Fáñez,
con esta presen[ta]ja adeliñó pora allá.
sentences.l:
Glad was of this Minaya Álbar Fáñez,
with this present he-headed for there.
sentences.i: Minaya Álvar Fáñez was glad of this, and with this present he made his way there.
sentences.n: f[o] = fue; aquesto = esto. Pidal's note to v. 1315: presentaja, 'presente, regalo', 'present, gift': the hundred horses of v. 1274. The ta of presen[ta]ja is Pidal's (in italics). pora allá, 'thither'.

sentences.t:
De missa era exido essora el rey Alfonsso,
afe Minaya Álbar Fáñez do llega tan apu[o]sto:
sentences.l:
From mass was gone-out then the king Alfonsso,
lo Minaya Álbar Fáñez where he-arrives so seemly:
sentences.i: King Alfonso had just come out from Mass, when behold Minaya Álvar Fáñez arriving in seemly fashion:
sentences.n: Tirada 81 (assonance ó-o) — Minaya greets the king (Pidal: Minaya saluda al rey). Line-ends Alfonsso, apu[o]sto, pu[o]blo, du[o]lo, apu[o]sto. The italic o of apu[o]sto, pu[o]blo, du[o]lo (and fu[o]rt, v. 1330) is Pidal's: he prints the older diphthong uo where modern Spanish has ue (apuesto, pueblo, duelo), which brings the stressed o of the assonance into the spelling; he gives no note here. era exido, 'had gone out': ser + the participle of a verb of motion (exir = salir). essora, 'just then' (v. 1282). afe, 'behold, lo', pointing at what comes next: afe Minaya … do llega, 'there is Minaya, arriving'. apu[o]sto, 'fitting, seemly', used as an adverb.

sentences.t:
fincó sos inojos ante tod el pu[o]blo,
a los pie[de]s del rey Alfons cayó con grand du[o]lo,
besávale las manos e fabló tan apu[o]sto:
sentences.l:
he-planted his knees before all the people,
at the feet of-the king Alfons he-fell with great grief,
he-was-kissing-him the hands and spoke so seemly:
sentences.i: he went down on his knees before all the people, fell at King Alfonso's feet with great sorrow, kissed his hands, and spoke in seemly words:
sentences.n: fincó sos inojos, 'planted his knees', knelt (fincar = hincar; inojos = hinojos; sos = sus), as at v. 53. tod el = todo el. pie[de]s, the old plural piedes, 'feet', its de Pidal's, as before. Alfons, the short form of Alfonsso. du[o]lo = duelo, 'grief, sorrow': the suppliant's show of feeling for his exiled lord. besávale, 'kissed him (the hands)', le the dative of the person; the imperfect among the preterites (fincó, cayó, fabló) is the poem's tense-mixing.

sentences.t:
“Merçed, señor Alfonsso, por amor del Criador!
Besávavos las manos mio Çid lidiador,
los pie[de]s e las manos, commo a tan buen señor,
quel ayades merçed, sí vos vala el Criador!
sentences.l:
“Mercy, lord Alfonsso, for love of-the Creator!
Was-kissing-you the hands my Çid fighter,
the feet and the hands, as to so good lord,
that-to-him you-may-have mercy, so you may-avail the Creator!
sentences.i: “Mercy, lord Alfonso, for the love of the Creator! My Çid the warrior kisses your hands — your feet and your hands, as befits so good a lord — and begs you to show him mercy, so may the Creator keep you!
sentences.n: Tirada 82 (assonance ó) — Minaya's speech to the king; Garci Ordóñez's envy; the king pardons the Çid's household; the Infantes of Carrión covet the Çid's riches (Pidal: Discurso de Minaya al rey. — Envidia de Garci Ordóñez. — El rey perdona a la familia del Cid. — Los infantes de Carrión codician las riquezas del Cid). The line-ends are a stressed ó (Criador, lidiador, señor, amor, so, miyor, Castejón …), with ó-e endings counting alongside (nombre, corredores, Ordóñez, omne, f[o]ren); on the italic final e of coraçon[e] and the rest see v. 1355. Merçed, 'mercy, grace', the petitioner's word (v. 266). Criador, 'Creator'. Besávavos = besava + vos, 'kissed you (the hands)': an imperfect, where v. 1338 has the present bésavos — perhaps the tense of a message entrusted ('he charged me to kiss'); the nuance is uncertain. Pidal's note to v. 1322: besavos las manos que …, 'os pide que', 'he asks you that' (compare v. 179): the kiss is the form of the request. lidiador, 'fighter'. pie[de]s, Pidal's de again. commo a tan buen señor, 'as (is due) to so good a lord'. quel = que le; ayades, present subjunctive 2nd pl. of aver: quel ayades merçed, 'that you have mercy on him'. sí vos vala el Criador, 'so may the Creator help you' (sí, 'so', the oath-formula; vala, present subjunctive of valer).

sentences.t:
Echástesle de tierra, non ha la vuestra amor;
maguer en tierra agena, él bien faze lo so:
sentences.l:
You-cast-him from land, not he-has the your love;
although in land foreign, he well does the his:
sentences.i: You cast him out of the land; he has lost your favour; yet, though in a foreign land, he does his part well:
sentences.n: Echástesle = echastes + le, preterite 2nd pl. of echar (= le echasteis): echar de tierra, the formula of banishment. ha = 'has' (aver, 'to have, hold'). amor is feminine here: la vuestra amor, with article + possessive. maguer, 'although'. agena = ajena, 'another's, foreign'. faze lo so, 'does what is his', most likely 'does his part well, acquits himself well'; the exact nuance is uncertain. so = su, suyo.

sentences.t:
ganada a Xérica e a Onda por nombre,
priso a Almenar e a Murviedro que es miyor,
assí fizo Çebolla e adelant Castejón,
e Peña Cadiella, que es una peña fu[o]rt;
sentences.l:
won Xérica and Onda by name,
he-took Almenar and Murviedro which is better,
so he-did Çebolla and further-on Castejón,
and Peña Cadiella, which is a crag strong;
sentences.i: he has won Jérica and Onda, as they are called; he took Almenara, and Murviedro, which is greater still; so too he did with Cebolla and, beyond it, Castellón, and Peña Cadiella, which is a mighty crag;
sentences.n: ganada a Xérica e a Onda: the participle agrees with the first place named and its auxiliary is left out, '(he has) won'; or the phrase stands on its own, 'Jérica won, and Onda' — either way the sense is plain (compare conquistas, v. 1092). a, the a set before town names as before persons. por nombre, 'by name', a filler for the half-line. Xérica = Jérica (x = [ʃ]), Almenar = Almenara: the towns of v. 1092. priso, old preterite of prender, 'took'. Murviedro, modern Sagunto (tirada 65). miyor = mejor, 'better, greater'. assí fizo Çebolla, 'so he did Cebolla', i.e. took it likewise (v. 1150); adelant, 'further on'. Pidal's note to v. 1329: Castejón is the Castilian pronunciation of the Valencian name Castellón de la Plana, formerly called Castellón de Burriana; this town, not named before, stands for the tierras de Borriana mentioned at v. 1093. Peña Cadiella, the stronghold of v. 1163. fu[o]rt = fuerte, its o Pidal's (as with apu[o]sto, v. 1317).

sentences.t:
con aquestas todas de Valençia es señor,
obispo fizo de su mano el buen Campeador,
e fizo çinco lides campales e todas las arrancó.
sentences.l:
with these all of Valençia he-is lord,
bishop made of his hand the good Campeador,
and he-made five battles pitched and all them he-won.
sentences.i: with all these he is lord of Valencia; the good Campeador has made a bishop with his own hand; and he has fought five pitched battles, and won them all.
sentences.n: aquestas todas, 'all these' (the places just named). de su mano, 'by his own hand', on his own authority (Pidal's note to v. 1302: the Cid makes the bishop himself). fizo … lides campales, 'fought pitched battles' (lid, 'battle'; campal, 'in the open field'). arrancar, 'to rout, win (a battle)': todas las arrancó, 'he won them all', las taking up lides. Pidal's note to v. 1333: the poet has told us of only two of these five battles.

sentences.t:
Grandes son las ganançias quel dio el Criador,
fevos aqui las señas, verdad vos digo yo:
sentences.l:
Great are the gains which-to-him gave the Creator,
behold-you here the tokens, truth to-you I-say I:
sentences.i: Great are the gains the Creator has given him; here you have the proof of them, I tell you truly:
sentences.n: quel = que le, 'which … (to) him'. fevos = fe + vos, 'behold, here for you' (fe, 'see, here is', as afe, v. 1317). señas, here most likely 'signs, tokens', the proof of the gains: the horses that follow — not the 'banners' nor the distributive señas, 'one each', met elsewhere; Pidal gives no note, and this reading is the sense that fits. aqui, unaccented in Pidal's print. verdad vos digo yo, 'I tell you the truth', the speaker's assurance.

sentences.t:
çient cavallos gruessos e corredores,
de siellas e de frenos todos guarnidos son,
bésavos las manos que los prendades vos;
razonas por vuestro vassallo e a vos tiene por señor.”
sentences.l:
a-hundred horses stout and swift,
with saddles and with bridles all furnished they-are,
he-kisses-you the hands that them you-may-take you;
he-declares-himself for your vassal and you he-holds for lord.”
sentences.i: a hundred horses, stout and swift, all furnished with saddles and bridles. He begs you to accept them; he declares himself your vassal and holds you as his lord.”
sentences.n: çient = cien. gruessos, 'stout, strong'; corredores, here an adjective, 'swift, fast-running' (not the 'raiders' of v. 1159). guarnidos, 'furnished, fitted out'. bésavos las manos que …, as at v. 1322; Pidal's note to v. 1338: 'os pide que los toméis', 'he asks you to take them' (v. 179). prendades, present subjunctive 2nd pl. of prender, 'to take'. razonas = razona se, 'speaks of himself as, declares himself', the se squeezed onto the verb. tener por, 'to hold as'. Banished and out of favour (v. 1325), the Çid still calls himself the king's man.

sentences.t:
Alçó la mano diestra, el rey se santigó:
“De tan fieras ganançias commo a fechas el Campeador
¡sí me vala sant Esidr[e]! plázme de coraçón.
sentences.l:
He-raised the hand right, the king himself crossed:
“Of so fierce gains as has made the Campeador
so me may-avail saint Esidr[e]! it-pleases-me from heart.
sentences.i: The king raised his right hand and crossed himself: “At such tremendous winnings as the Campeador has made — so help me Saint Isidore! — I am glad with all my heart,
sentences.n: se santigó, 'crossed himself', here in wonder. fieras, 'huge, astonishing' (fiero, 'fierce', as an intensive). a fechas = ha fechas, 'has made', aver + participle agreeing with ganançias (fechas = hechas, f- for h-). De tan fieras ganançias, put first, depends on plázme: 'I am pleased at such …'. sí me vala sant Esidr[e], 'so may Saint Isidore help me', the oath-formula of v. 1324; the final e is Pidal's. Pidal's note to v. 1342: sant Esidre is Saint Isidore, bishop of Seville from 599 to 636, whom the king often invokes in the poem (vv. 1867, 3028, 3140); Alfonso VI's devotion to him was inherited from his father Fernando I, who in 1063 moved the saint's body from Seville to León; hence he is called sant Esidro el de León (v. 3509). plázme = plaze me, 'it pleases me', the e of plaze dropped; de coraçón, 'from the heart'.

sentences.t:
e plázem de las nuevas que faze el Campeador;
reçibo estos cavallos quem enbía de don.”
sentences.l:
and it-pleases-me of the deeds which does the Campeador;
I-receive these horses which-to-me he-sends of gift.”
sentences.i: and I rejoice in the deeds the Campeador performs; I accept these horses he sends me as a gift.”
sentences.n: plázem = plaze me again, now with the e of me dropped instead: the same words squeezed the other way. Pidal's note to v. 1343: las nuevas que faze, 'las hazañas que hace', 'the exploits he performs' (nuevas, elsewhere 'news, renown', here the deeds that make it). quem = que me, 'which … (to) me'. de don, 'as a gift'.

sentences.t:
Maguer plogo al rey, mucho pesó a Garci Ordóñez:
“Semeja que en tierra de moros non a bivo omne,
quando assí faze a su guisa el Çid Campeador!”
sentences.l:
Although it-pleased to-the king, much it-weighed to Garci Ordóñez:
“It-seems that in land of Moors not there-is living man,
when thus does at his way the Çid Campeador!”
sentences.i: But though it pleased the king, it weighed heavily on Garci Ordóñez: “It seems there is not a man left alive in the land of the Moors, when the Çid Campeador does just as he pleases there!”
sentences.n: Maguer, 'although'. plogo, preterite of plazer; pesar a uno, 'to grieve, vex someone'. Garci Ordóñez is named here for the first time in the surviving text: a count (al co[m]de, v. 1348) of Alfonso's court, and plainly the Çid's ill-wisher. Pidal's note to v. 1345 refers to his introduction on him, and observes that the coldness with which the king treats the count here goes against historical reality. Semeja, 'it seems'. non a bivo omne, 'there is no living man': a = ha, impersonal aver, 'there is'; bivo = vivo; omne = hombre. a su guisa, 'after his own fashion, as he pleases'. The sneer makes the Çid's victories cheap, as if no Moor were left to stand against him.

sentences.t:
Dixo el rey al co[m]de: “dexad essa razón,
que en todas guisas mijor me sirve que vos.”
sentences.l:
Said the king to-the count: “leave-ye that talk,
for in all ways better me he-serves than you.”
sentences.i: The king said to the count: “Leave that talk; for in every way he serves me better than you.”
sentences.n: co[m]de = conde, 'count', its m Pidal's. dexad, imperative 2nd pl. of dexar (= dejad). razón, 'talk, words'. que, 'for'. en todas guisas, 'in every way'. mijor = mejor (miyor at v. 1328: two spellings of one word).

sentences.t: Fablava Minaya i a guisa de varón:
sentences.l: Was-speaking Minaya there in manner of man:
sentences.i: Minaya spoke up there, like the true man he was:
sentences.n: Fablava, an imperfect where a preterite is expected: tense-mixing again (fablar = hablar). i = 'there'. a guisa de varón, 'in the manner of a man', boldly and well; varón, 'man, a true man'.

sentences.t:
“merçed vos pide el Çid, si vos ca[d]iesse en sabor,
por su mugier doña Ximena e sus fijas amas a dos
saldríen del monesterio do elle las dexó,
e irién pora Valençia al buen Campeador.”
sentences.l:
“mercy of-you asks the Çid, if to-you it-should-fall into liking,
for his wife doña Ximena and his daughters both two
they-would-go-out from-the monastery where he them left,
and they-would-go to Valençia to-the good Campeador.”
sentences.i: “The Çid asks a favour of you, if it should be your pleasure: for his wife Doña Ximena and both his daughters, that they might come out of the monastery where he left them and go to Valencia, to the good Campeador.”
sentences.n: merçed vos pide, 'asks a grace of you'. Pidal's note to v. 1351: si vos cadiese en sabor, 'si os pluguiese', 'if it pleased you' (compare v. 313): ca[d]iesse, imperfect subjunctive of caer, 'should fall', its d Pidal's; en sabor, 'into liking'. por su mugier …: the persons are named first and the sentence then runs on with them as the subject of saldríen, 'as for his wife … (that) they might come out'. amas a dos, 'both (the) two'. saldríen, irién: conditional 3rd pl. (= saldrían, irían), the -ien ending. monesterio, San Pedro de Cardeña (v. 1285). elle = él, 'he'. dexó = dejó.

sentences.i: Then the king said: “It pleases me with all my heart. I will have provisions given them while they are in my land, and have them guarded from outrage, from harm and from dishonour;
sentences.n: Plazme = plaze me (unaccented here in Pidal's print; plázme at v. 1342). The italic final e of coraçon[e] and desonor[e] (and of Campeador[e], v. 1359) is Pidal's addition: the 'paragogic' e (his term, e paragógica, note to v. 1385), an extra vowel after the final consonant at the line-end, which turns these ó endings into ó-e. mandaré dar, 'I will order (them) to be given'; conducho, 'provisions'. mientra que = mientras, 'while'; f[o]ren = fueren, future subjunctive of ser, its o Pidal's. Pidal's note to v. 1356: 'I will order supplies given them while they travel through my kingdom, and curiarlas, guard them, from affront'; the king promises to protect the ladies through the whole extent of his kingdom, as a lord was bound to do for his vassal (compare vv. 3476–79), for the outrages of powerful counts and infanzones were a constant danger. curial[l]as = curiar + las, the r of the infinitive becoming l before las; the second l is Pidal's. fonta, 'outrage, affront'.

sentences.t:
quando en cabo de mi tierra aquestas dueñas f[o]ren,
catad cómmo las sirvades vos e el Campeador[e].
sentences.l:
when at end of my land these ladies shall-be,
see-ye how them you-may-serve you and the Campeador.
sentences.i: when these ladies reach the bounds of my land, see to it how you serve them, you and the Campeador.
sentences.n: en cabo de, 'at the end, the edge of'. aquestas dueñas, 'these ladies' (dueña, a lady of rank). f[o]ren, future subjunctive again. catad, imperative 2nd pl. of catar, 'look, see to it'. sirvades, present subjunctive 2nd pl. of servir. Beyond his frontier, the king says, their care is yours.

sentences.i: Hear me, my household knights, and all my court! I would not have the Campeador lose anything: to all the knights who call him lord, whom for that I stripped of their lands, I release everything;
sentences.n: Oídme, imperative + me. Pidal's note to v. 1360: escuelas, schola regis in Latin texts, corresponds to the scholae palatinae, the palace guards of the Roman empire; in general escuelas is the same as mesnadas, the body of a lord's vassals, whether the king's or the Cid's (vv. 1362, 2072) — not 'schools'. la mi cort, article + possessive. que nada pierda, 'that he lose anything' (pierda, present subjunctive of perder). a él dizen señor, 'call him lord'. por que los deseredé, 'for which I disinherited them', stripped them of their lands for following him (deseredar = desheredar). todo gelo suelto yo, 'I release it all to them' (ge lo, 'to them it'; soltar, 'to let go, remit').

sentences.t:
sírvanle' sus her[e]dades do f[o]re el Campeador,
atrégoles los cuerpos de mal e de ocasión,
por tal fago aquesto que sirvan a so señor.”
sentences.i: let them keep their estates wherever the Campeador may be; I guarantee their persons against harm and mischance; and this I do so that they may serve their lord.”
sentences.n: sírvanle': Pidal prints the apostrophe, and his note to v. 1364 writes sírvanles sus heredades, so it apparently marks the s of les, lost before the s of sus. sírvanles, present subjunctive of servir with les, 'let their estates serve them': Pidal glosses 'queden en posesión de ellas, aunque ausentes', 'let them remain in possession of them, though absent', and cites the phrase frequent in charters and fueros, serviat ei sua hereditas ubicumque voluerit esse, 'let his inheritance serve him wherever he will be'; the king's pardon, he adds, refers chiefly to the 115 knights who went with the Cid of their own will (v. 289). her[e]dades, the second e Pidal's. do f[o]re, 'wherever (he) may be', future subjunctive. Pidal's note to v. 1365: atrégoles, 'atréguoles', 'I assure them that they will suffer no harm nor ocasión', ocasión being 'serious damage'. los cuerpos, 'their persons'. por tal … que, 'for this end, that'. fago = hago; so = su.

sentences.t:
Minaya Álbar Fáñez las manos le besó.
Sonrrisós el rey, tan vellido fabló:
sentences.l:
Minaya Álbar Fáñez the hands to-him kissed.
Smiled-himself the king, so handsome he-spoke:
sentences.i: Minaya Álvar Fáñez kissed his hands. The king smiled, and spoke most graciously:
sentences.n: las manos le besó, 'kissed his hands', le the dative of the person. Sonrrisós = sonrrisó se, 'smiled' (sonrrisar, v. 1266). Pidal's note to v. 1368: vellido, an adjective used as an adverb, 'hermosamente', 'beautifully, graciously'.

sentences.t:
“Los que quisieren ir se[r]vir al Campeador
de mí sean quitos e vayan a la graçia del Criador.
Más ganaremos en esto que en otra des[amor].”
sentences.l:
“Those who may-wish to-go to-se[r]ve to-the Campeador
of me let-them-be quit and let-them-go to the grace of-the Creator.
More we-shall-gain in this than in other dis[favour].”
sentences.i: “Those who wish to go and serve the Campeador, let them be quit of me, and go with the Creator's grace. We shall gain more by this than by further ill will.”
sentences.n: quisieren, future subjunctive of querer, 'shall wish'. ir se[r]vir, ir + bare infinitive, 'go (and) serve'; the r is Pidal's. de mí sean quitos, 'let them be quit of me', released from their duty to the king (quito, 'free, discharged'); sean, vayan, present subjunctives of command. a la graçia del Criador, 'with God's grace', a blessing on departure. otra des[amor]: the amor is in italics, Pidal's restoration, and he gives no note. Read as 'than by any other (course of) ill will', i.e. than by keeping up the enmity; desamor, 'ill will, disfavour', feminine like amor (v. 1325). The restored word and the sense of the line are uncertain. ganaremos, future 1st pl. of ganar: the king counts himself among the gainers.

sentences.t:
Aquí entraron en fabla iffantes de Carrión:
“Mucho creçen las nuevas de mio Çid el Campeador,
bien casariemos con sus fijas pora huebos de pro.
sentences.l:
Here entered into talk infantes of Carrión:
“Much grow the tidings of my Çid the Campeador,
well we-would-marry with his daughters for need of profit.
sentences.i: At this the Infantes of Carrión fell to talking together: “The fame of my Çid the Campeador grows mightily; it would be a good match for us to marry his daughters, to our own advantage.
sentences.n: Pidal's note to v. 1372: the Infantes of Carrión, more noble than rich, begin to covet the Cid's wealth on seeing the magnificent presents the exile sends to Castile (compare vv. 1835, 1864, 1881, 1888). iffantes, spelled with ff: here not 'children' (as the Çid's daughters at v. 1279) but young men of noble birth, sons of the counts of Carrión (v. 1376). entrar en fabla, 'to fall to talking', between themselves. creçen las nuevas, 'the renown grows'. casariemos, conditional 1st pl. of casar (= casaríamos), the -iemos ending: bien casariemos, 'we would marry well'. Pidal's note to v. 1374: pora huebos de pro, 'para atender a nuestro provecho', 'to look to our own profit' (compare v. 1461); huebos, 'need'; pro, 'profit'.

sentences.t:
Non la osariemos acometer nos esta razón.
Mio Çid es de Bivar e nos de co[m]des de Carrión.”
Non lo dizen a nadi, e fincó esta razón.
sentences.l:
Not it we-would-dare to-propose we this matter.
My Çid is of Bivar and we of counts of Carrión.”
Not it they-say to anyone, and remained this matter.
sentences.i: But we would not dare to put this forward: my Çid is of Vivar, and we are of the counts of Carrión.” They say it to no one, and there the matter rested.
sentences.n: Pidal's note to v. 1375: 'No osaríamos proponer este proyecto', 'we would not dare to propose this plan'. Non la … esta razón: the object announced by la and then named (razón, 'matter, proposal'). osariemos, conditional 1st pl. of osar; acometer, here 'to broach, put forward'; nos = nosotros, 'we', the subject (not the reflexive). co[m]des = condes, its m Pidal's. Pidal's note to v. 1376: for the Infantes the inequality of the two lineages stood out from the mere contrast of the names of the places from which the two houses took their names: Vivar was a village, Carrión a city, the head of a county; in reality the lineage of the counts of Carrión, the Beni-Gómez, was very illustrious. Why they would not dare, the lines leave unsaid; Pidal reads it in that inequality of birth. nadi = nadie; Non … a nadi, double negative. fincó esta razón, 'this matter stayed (as it was)', went no further for now (fincar, 'to remain').

sentences.i: Minaya Álvar Fáñez took his leave of the good king. “Are you going already, Minaya? Go with the Creator's grace! Take a royal officer with you; I think he will be of use to you;
sentences.n: se espidió, 'took his leave' (espedirse). Hya = ya, spelled with h. ides = vais; id, imperative 2nd pl. of ir. Levedes, present subjunctive 2nd pl. of levar, 'you should take'. Pidal's note to v. 1380: about the eleventh century the portero replaced the old royal sayón or executor of the Visigothic period and the first centuries of the Reconquest: a palace official charged at first with bringing persons into the monarch's presence, then with carrying the king's letters or orders and carrying out his commands (compare vv. 1536–39, 2962–63). So not a door-keeper but the king's officer, travelling with the king's authority. tengo que, 'I hold that, I think'. avrá pro, 'will be of profit'; avrá = habrá, future of aver.

sentences.t:
si leváredes las dueñas, sírvanlas a su sabor,
fata dentro en Medina denles quanto huebos les f[o]r,
desí adelant piensse dellas el Campeador.”
Espidiós Minaya e vasse de la cort.
sentences.l:
if you-should-take the ladies, let-them-serve-them at their liking,
as-far-as inside in Medina let-them-give-them as-much-as need to-them may-be,
thence forward let-take-thought of-them the Campeador.”
Took-leave-himself Minaya and goes-himself from the court.
sentences.i: if you bring the ladies, let them be served as they please; as far as Medinaceli let them be given whatever they need; from there on, let the Campeador look after them.” Minaya took his leave, and goes from the court.
sentences.n: leváredes, future subjunctive 2nd pl. of levar, 'if you should take'. sírvanlas, denles: present subjunctives of command with an unnamed 'they' (the king's people along the road), 'let them serve them', 'let them give them'. a su sabor, 'to their liking'. fata = hasta, 'as far as'; dentro en, 'right into'. Pidal's note to v. 1382: quanto huebos les for, 'cuanto necesitaren', 'whatever they may need' (v. 123): huebos, 'need'; f[o]r = fuere, the future subjunctive of ser cut to one syllable, its o Pidal's. Medina is Medinaceli, a city lately conquered by Alfonso and the farthest limit of his kingdoms. desí adelant, 'from there onward'. piensse, present subjunctive of pensar: pensar de, 'to take care of'. dellas = de ellas. Espidiós = espidió se; vasse = va se, 'goes off': preterite and present side by side to close the tirada. cort = corte, 'court'.
